subject: Human Evolution
title: Isotopes and Ancient Diets
description: A fast breakdown of Isotopes and Ancient Diets for builders.

hook.text: You are what you eat—and so were our ancestors. Their teeth recorded every meal in chemical signatures.

buildup.text: Carbon isotopes in tooth enamel differ between C3 plants (fruits, leaves) and C4 plants (grasses, sedges).

discovery.text: Australopithecus ate mainly C3 foods. Later hominins shifted to C4—showing a move to open grasslands.

twist.text: Strontium isotopes reveal where an individual grew up, tracking migration across different geologies.

climax.text: A single tooth can reveal what someone ate, where they lived, and when they moved—millions of years later.

punchline.text: Teeth are time capsules of ancient lives.

quiz.question: What do carbon isotopes in teeth reveal?
options: Type of diet (forest vs. grassland foods)
